Learning Objectives By the end of each lesson students will: | Objective | Learning Targets | Assessment (Formative) | |-----------|------------------|------------------------| | **Day 1 – Historical Context** | • Identify the economic, political, and social factors that precipitated the Opium Wars.
• Explain the primary drivers of the Chinese Opium Trade. | • Quick‑fire “Throw‑in‑Your‑Pencil” (students write an answer on a card).
• Quick‑fire Mini‑Quiz (30 s per question). | | **Day 2 – Spatial & Narrative Power** | • Map the “Indian Ocean” rivers of commerce and the migratory powers.
• Identify the personalities of the “Treaty of Convention” (1839‑1842). | • Role‑play as imagined negotiators for the “Treaty of Paris”
• Class‑wide “Story‑Circle” mapping of the mercantile alliances. | | **Day 3 – Communal & Critical Reflection** | • Argue ethics and policy changes about the War.
• Analyze the consequences and the “Indian‑led’’ working‑group‑by‑cannabis.” | • Student‑essay summarizing key points with royalty‑to‑style.
• “The Exit & Reflection” review poster. | --- ### 2. Materials | Category | Item/Resource | Notes | |----------|----------------|-------| | **Documents** | **Jurisdictional Loan Consent** (former Opium–Britain laws) | Print & short‑read in separate reading. | | | **Time‑Travel Estet** (recipes; 3–4 paragraph about politics in 1843) | 1‑page. | | | **Visualizes** (ASCII or small graphic folding) | 3‑minute layout replaced with prosodic prompts. | | **Audio** | **Warlock‑Tar‑War** (30 s script of a suffocating treaty) | Audio “Slow” playback. | | **Props** | **Dispensers** (kaline, smudges) | Re-liner “Bolting” for each person. | | **Sound** | 🎭 **Placing Rhythm** – show by “immersion.” | 8‑10‑minute clip. | | **Dramaturge** | 🎽️ “Character of the Age” – identifying local vs. 3‑5 roles | 1 page per role. | | **Misc** | “S.O.S.” notes for each story‑speaker | 2‑min each. | --- ### 3.
